To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the phosphorylation of eIF- 2alpha in adenovirus- infected cells is due to the activation of a cellular protein kinase (DAI) by the virus, 2) DAI is required for the selective translation of adenoviral mRNA and the shut- off of host cell protein translation, and 3) the virus has evolved a mechanism to inhibit DAI activity by the production of the VA RNAI.

(1) VA RNA is required to prevent phosphorylation of the initiation factor eIF2 alpha in adenovirus infected cells; (2) eIF-2 phosphorylation increases in adenovirus- infected cells at late times; (3) eIF- 2 phosphorylation is required for host protein synthesis shut- off in adenovirus infection
VA RNAI is not essential for the phosphorylation of the initiation factor, eIF- 2 alpha, in adenovirus infected cells, and that DAI is required for efficient host shut-off in adenovirus infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which viruses regulate host and viral gene expression.
the molecular mechanisms of viral gene expression and the regulation of host cell protein production.
the mechanisms by which adenoviruses control the expression of host and viral genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VA RNAI and DAI are involved in a complex mechanism that is essential for normal viral growth.
adenovirus infection results in the selective activation of DAI, which phosphorylates eIF-2, thereby shutting off host protein synthesis.
VA RNAI prevents eIF-2 phosphorylation by DAI at early times of infection, and that the same system is involved in shut-off at late times.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VA RNAI and DAI are required to regulate the shut-off of protein synthesis in adenova infected cells, but the mechanism by which this is achieved is not as simple as was originally envisioned.
VA RNAI is required for the efficient translation of late viral mRNA, and that this function is mediated through the regulation of eIF-4A.
the mechanism of host protein synthesis shut off in adenovirus infected cells is the phosphorylation of eIF- 2 alpha.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adenovirus DAI protein and VA RNAI play an important role in the selective translation and shut-off of host mRNA during late infection.
the mechanism for host protein synthesis shut off during adenovirus infection is more complex than originally thought, involving the selective translation of mRNA from the host and the virus.
the shut-off of cellular protein synthesis is not due to the inhibition of eIF-4F activity by the adenovirus L4 22K protein.
